TOTAL DEBT for FY2024 is $548,241, and $846,635 + $120,310 = $966,945, so the TOTAL DEBT cell is $418,704 LOW; it is GRAND TOTAL PRINCIPAL plus GRAND TOTAL INTEREST less that one payment. The same exclusion is carried into the TOTAL column: $27,097,991 + $9,263,504 = $36,361,495 against a printed TOTAL DEBT of $35,942,791, short by the same $418,704; and the issue's own printed total, $5,651,592, is the sum of its TWELVE printed year totals (FY2012-FY2023) while its printed principal total $4,580,191 includes the thirteenth year. Every one of those relations closes to the dollar. WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: why. A final principal payment with no interest due, a total formula that stopped one column short, and a payment entered in the wrong row all fit the figures identically, and nothing on these two pages distinguishes them. IT IS NOT FY2015'S EXCLUSION. FY2015's printed grand totals leave TWO WHOLE school-construction issues out of every year column ($29.6M of $49.6M). Here one CELL in one year of one issue is missing from two derived rows, and the arithmetic locates it exactly. It DOES match what FY2013 and FY2014 both show -- a `MASS WATER POOL 9*` row with a principal and no interest or total -- so the same issue prints the same way in three consecutive reports. closes: the Treasurer's MWPAT loan amortisation schedule for pool 9, which is not published.
